utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before I ask for the appearances, I note for the record that we reconvene this morning under Rule 15 bis, Judge Delvoie being absent. Yes, may have I the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Matthew Olmsted, Joanna Korner, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic, appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before the witness is recalled to the stand, in respect of the outstanding motion by the Prosecution as to whether the witness Riedlmayer, who is scheduled to testify next week, would be classified as an expert witness, we have decided that we will so treat him, and our written reasons will follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm very grateful. Can we say, Mr. Hannis will be leading the witness, and I understand he is going to discuss with the Defence the parameters of the testimony. We will be limiting - can I make this absolutely clear - part of the -- the opinion evidence he can give to matters that we hope will be non-contentious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You have two hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I believe we asked for two hours, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may I have a correction to the transcript with regards to the numbers assigned yesterday on page 10953. The number -- the documents tendered by the Prosecution will be assigned the exhibit numbers P1386 through P1392 because two of them are already admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic, good morning to you. Before Mr. Olmsted --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before Mr. Olmsted winds up his examination-in-chief, I remind you you're still on your oath. Yes, Mr. Olmsted. You have one thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Radulovic.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you recall attending the Security Day Parade in Banja Luka in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the capacity of an operative.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: During your proofing, you had an opportunity to review a -- some video footage, and I want to show that to you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We're going to bring it up on Sanction, and it's 65 ter 3596.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We are about 3 minutes -- 34 minutes and 48 seconds into this video. Mr. Radulovic, we're looking at a number of armoured personnel carriers and tanks that are painted blue. Do you recognise these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can I recognise them. As far as I know, the armaments, the equipment, and the logistics were those of the JNA. It was probably given to the police, and we only painted those vehicles. These vehicles were not manufactured for the police. They were taken from the arsenals of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Did you see the Banja Luka special police detachment using vehicles such as these?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And where would you see them in use, in operation?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether there were any other special units with such vehicles, but I did see such blue vehicles in the area of Prijedor and Kotor Varos. One of these was even in Teslic during the operation when we confronted the Mice Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's fast-forward to 49 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic, we're looking at three men in uniform about to give a review of a number of police officers. And I want to see if you can recognise, identify the three men. We'll pause it at a point here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Tell us if you recognise any of them.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, there's Stojan Zupljanin. There's the late Stevan Markovic. I cannot be certain, but I think there's also Mr. Mico Stanisic, the one in military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move ahead to -- by the way, do you know where this review is taking place? Could you tell us where it is?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location is easily recognizable to anyone who was in Banja Luka. This is the square in front of the Boska department store. Even today most mass rallies take place there. Yeah, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's move ahead to 52 minutes and 10 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic, can you identify who is coming out of the door here?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise for what I'm about to say, because -- this is a kind of a funny question because everybody would recognise Mr. Radovan Karadzic and there's also Krajisnik. But I understand that you need confirmation. In the background, I can see an employee of the former SJB. He was later director of a power station and -- but he died in the meantime from a tumour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We just saw a man with greyish hair and a pointy beard. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I recognise Predrag Radic. He is turned towards the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And the man in the suit with the -- with the beard?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, him. Yes. It's clearer to me now. This is Dr. Vukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's play a little further.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Who else do you recognise in this lineup?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there's Predrag Radic next to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Keep on playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's fast-forward to 55:05 -- 55 minutes and 5 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you recognise the man at the far end in the camouflage? Is that someone you can identify?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Maybe back a little.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is Mr. Mico Stanisic. Well, I can see him here in the courtroom too. I'm not sure that's him, because it's been a long time. But as far as can I tell, this is Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's go to 55 minutes and 33 seconds.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So Mico Stanisic is the first and then Predrag Radic, then Vukic, Karadzic, and Krajisnik. These are all the people we can see in this still image.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you. Who's -- who's that next to Mr. Stanisic, to the right of him?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Milan Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 55 minutes and 44 seconds, and we're going to --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you recognise the man to the right of Mr. Martic?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I remember seeing him, but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And who is the man, you can see him in the second row, you just see his head. He's between Mr. Martic and Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Nedeljko Kesic, the chief of the National Security Service in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's go to 55 minutes and 44 seconds. And we're just going to play the speech of Mr. Stanisic. It's quite short.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's stop it and restart it. If the interpreters could translate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: "[VOICEOVER]: On St. George's Day many Serb families were rooted out in the area of Srebrenica. The Muslims say many were breaking in houses, killing hosts together with their guests and burning down houses. The situations were not rare when Serbs were used as human shields or they deployed them in strategic spots for which they believed that could be the target of our attacks. There are equally numerous examples, you are all aware of them on your own territories, so there's no need to quote them further. The service gathered intelligence that they are trying to establish some private ... on the particular territories of the Serb republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina which are targeting the Serbian people and everyone living in the territory of the Serb republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. With the arrival of freedom what expects us, although we can say that outside the appearance of the situation in the territory of the Serb republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is satisfactory, we have to take into conversation that the service gathered numerous facts that are indicating ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Okay. And now we are at 56 minutes and 57 seconds, and we're not going to have this speech interpreted, but could you tell us, Mr. Radulovic, who is speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And just could you repeat who is the speaker. I don't know if the record picked it up.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I can see Mr. Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And just, very quickly, if we can go to 1 minute -- or 1 hour, 6 minutes, and 5 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, of course, who is now giving a speech?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in this still image I can see Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's go to 1 minute -- or 1 hour, 14 minutes and 32 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now what we see in front of us appears to be a meeting and on the -- what is displayed on this footage is the date, 30 July 1992. Can we skip ahead to 1 hour 5 minutes and 11 seconds?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And perhaps you can identify, Mr. Radulovic, who is heading this meeting?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see Stojan Zupljanin and Djuro Bulic, if you mean the people sitting at that table, chairing the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Where is this meeting taking place?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with certainty. I can suppose that it -- this is in the CSB building of Banja Luka because I see green tablecloths that we used to use in our building in this hall on the fourth floor, or maybe on the third. I'm not sure which floor it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can you tell us, do you know who is speaking right now? If you don't know, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see anybody speaking; that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I see now. I know him from sight, but I really don't know the man's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you remember what municipality he is from?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can see next to him Vladimir Tutus.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now during your proofing --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about the municipality. I'm sorry, sir. You asked me if I could identify the municipality from which he was, and as far as I remember, he was from Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Radulovic, during your proofing you had an opportunity to review the -- I don't think the whole meeting but quite a bit of it and it goes for quite a length. But, generally, who are the participants at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me first say that I didn't have a position in the service by virtue of which I would attend such meetings. But I was able to recognise most of the people, and, thus, I can draw the conclusions that they were the chiefs of the police stations from the Banja Luka region.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Were any -- when you review this footage, did you see any of your superiors in state security?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them now in the background. There's Vojin Bera. He's sitting next to the Prijedor chief, Vladan Vesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The Prijedor SJB chief, is that who you said?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, Vladan Vesic. It's actually Gradiska, I misspoke. It's Gradiska. Mr. Vladan Vesic was the chief from Gradiska, and I can see him sitting next to Bera, Vojin Bera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What colour of the shirt is he wearing, Mr. Bera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is he wearing a white shirt. We can see him in profile. And he's wearing glasses, as far as can I see. So he's the chief of the police station in Gradiska. His naming is Vladan Vesic. In front of him, half his face is covered but can I recognise him anyway, also dressed in a white shirt, there's Vojin Bera.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And just for the record that's at 1 hour, 16 minutes and 46 seconds. Can we move ahead to 1 hour, 24 minutes and 30 seconds -- or I -- yeah, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Who is standing up right now, right in the front, right there?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, this is the head of Nedeljko Kesic. And on the right, I see a man whose name I think was about Brane Bukovac. He was head of the criminal investigations department. Behind him there's the chief of fire security at the CSB in Banja Luka. Next to him there's Skundric, I believe. Vaso was his first name. He had a position in the police inspectorate. And on the left I just said that this man recently died, died of a tumour. He was in the service, and later on, he was the manager of a power plant in Banja Luka. And behind him, I can't really recognise who these other people are.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That's fine. Let's go ahead to 1 hour, 26 minutes, and 12 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We see a man who's got his back to us wearing camouflage and his head is slightly profiled. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the one whose face is turned toward us is the chief from Jajce. And the one we see from the back is Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: May this exhibit be tendered into evidence. We have the transcripts from the other speeches as well as the transcripts from the speeches made at this meeting as well. Of course, we're not going to play those at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1393, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Just to clarify, both the video and the transcripts are -- are admitted? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That's what I thought [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Radulovic.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic, you're a member -- or you have been a member of the Ministry of the Interior since 1976.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since November 1976.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Mr. Radulovic, especially with cross-examination by counsel who speak the same language as you, it is necessary to allow a pause between question and answer so the interpreters can keep up and we have an accurate record. Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistake you worked for the intermunicipal SUP of Doboj, which is approximately like the CSB nowadays, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just make a pause between my question and your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You worked in public security until 1981, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In 1981, you went from public security to state security, also at the intermunicipal SUP of Doboj; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's partly correct. Because the State Security Service was not organised to be under the authority of the intermunicipal SUP. Instead, it was directly linked to the level of the republic, or directly below the level of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So, as opposed to the public security, it had direct links with the republican level; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since 1983, I believe, you have dealt specifically with matters concerning sects, NGOs, and the like?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Owing to your knowledge of these matters, you established contacts with the federal State Security Service, the military security, and the state security of Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. But also contacts with representatives of the services in other republics of the then Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In 1987 you were transferred from Doboj to Banja Luka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Upon your arrival in Banja Luka, you remained inspector of the SDB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Between 1987 and your transfer to Banja Luka, what matters were the main focus of your work?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Intelligence matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That -- these are the matters that are mainly dealt by the 01 administration of the security service, the intelligence matters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me after the multi-party elections in 1990, certain changes, or re-shuffling of positions which followed the pattern of relations between different parties, and that happened within the SDB as well; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: My question related practically to the entire organisation of the state, in all segments of society, including the Ministry of the Interior, this re-shuffling occurred.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, not one single segment remained without certain type of changes occurring based on this principle that you put forward; namely, the national principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you're a Communist by your beliefs, and you did not agree with these ethnic or national parties and their programmes, not even on the idealogical level; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct. These are my views still today. I'm still a Communist.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There's no point in asking you whether you were a member of any of the national parties.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was always member of the League of Communists, and at the moment, I'm the president of the association of Communists in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I'm proud to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In accordance to this coalition agreement between the parties that won the elections in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1990, appointments to leading positions in the MUP were, according to the law, done by the minister of the interior, Alija Delimustafic. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I know about this only in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, isn't it, that, according to a decision by the minister at the time, Mr. Delimustafic, CSB Banja Luka chief, then security service chief, Nedeljko Kesic and your boss, Vojin Bera, were also appointed?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it should have been like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that back in 1991, they were appointed to these positions by the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. That's how the procedure looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, it is a fact, isn't it, that Ljuban Ecim and Zdravko Samardzija were also members of MUP back in 1991, maybe even before that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that. If you want specifically, Ecim joined public security service in 1987 or 1988 or maybe even earlier, whereas, Samardzija joined during the 1980s.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So both of them signed the contract or became part of MUP at the time while it was still MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Radulovic, this Milos [Realtime transcript read in error "Mice"] Group, if I understood it well, it was operative intelligence group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And if I remember your testimony, this group was established on the 28th of July, 1991. You told us that specific date.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think during the first day of your testimony you confirmed that this operative intelligence group was established in co-operation with the SDB of Serbia, and I think that, on Tuesday, in your testimony, you stressed, although it may have not been recorded in the record, that it was in direct contact with State Security Service and not with the public security service or MUP of Serbia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That was done because, I assume, there was a need to ensure secrecy of your work and the matter of your contacts with Serbian security service.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. However, that was not the only reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, there may be a matter that is not properly recorded, and Mr. Zecevic might want to clarify it. I'm looking at page 15, line 20, the question is: Thank you, Mr. Radulovic. This Mice Group. I'm not sure Mr. Zecevic said Mice Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Here on page 15, line 20, it is stated Mice Group, and we were talking about the Milos Group.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Milos Group. I would like to ask for that to be immediately corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is already.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, it is a fact, isn't, it, and I'm saying this for the purpose of showing you the context, on the 20th of July, 1991, the Republic of Slovenia and the Republic of Croatia already seceded from the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I assumed that may have been one of the reasons why your operative intelligence group was not linked up with the federal State Security Service but instead with the Serbian one because the federal State Security Service, after the cessation of the two republics, broke up along the ethnic lines. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us try and illustrate the situation in late 1991 and early 1992 on the basis of your reports. I would first like to ask you to comment on the document, P1353, item 25. It is a document that was shown to one of the witnesses before your turn, and we tried to help the Trial Chamber to clarify the situation. Madam Korner opposed this at the time, saying that the author of the document would come as a witness, and that you would be a better person to clarify the situation. Since she didn't do it, I will do it now. Sir, this document is dated 13th of April, 1992. The -- it says Milos in the signature. Do you remember the document?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I remember it excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain in brief what the problem was and what was the reason for this memo.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- this is a department store that could provide weapons to people who had proper documents, and I'm talking about personal weapons and hunting rifles. And among those who made payments were people of various ethnic groups. As far as I can remember, most of them were even Bosniaks. Since I knew the general manager of this department store, and bearing in mind that the payments were already made, it wasn't, of course, important how we knew each other, what I did was I asked Belgrade to deliver the weapons to the department store Merkur by the Promet Zastava company in order to avoid already existing problems, problems existing because the weapons were already paid for but were not delivered. I personally -- or, rather, the Milos Group was escorting and providing security for the weapons that were brought from Belgrade to Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact that Zastava Promet was one of the biggest organisations related to the manufacturer of personal weapons. Zastava Kragujevac, which according to regulation, was authorised to trade and sell hunting weapons and personal weapons, small-arms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In any case, during normal conditions in the country, in the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, transport of weapons of such sort would involve some security issues; namely, there would be a security escort with delivery, with the supply?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mainly if larger amounts were being transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D00-2804 on the screen, tab 55. Page 4, please. First, first page and then fourth page. Because I would like to ask the witness to verify that he's the author of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a report. You will see the last page. There it is stated that the date was the 4th of June, 1992, signed by Milos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 4 of the document in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see it. I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is it -- is the document yours?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can recognise the document as a Milos document. But evenly without Milos, I could recognise it based on the typeset of the typewriter. It's a very specific one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have, again, the first page of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In this report of yours, you report that current information point out to certain facts that may have not been familiar to -- at certain period of time. You said on 10th of June, 1991 SDA held in the police building in Sarajevo the -- held a meeting discussing strategy of formation of independent Bosnia and Herzegovina, formed national security council and started preparations for an armed conflict. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, Mr. Zecevic, these were not my first information about arming and paramilitary organisation of the SDA party. I provided first information about that in 1989, when I received first information that certain armed formations were established in the area of Sasine. You must understand that this contains only information I had in relation to 1992. This does not refer to intelligence starting in 1989. At the time, I -- correction, 1987, when I reported about same thing in the area of Republic of Croatia. And that's when I started reporting about it, because I realized there's a threat to my country, Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, that coming up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't have these reports of yours. What we have disclosed is only your reports signed by Milos and those reports related to 1992, and this is what I'm showing to you. But in any case, the report submitted by you was --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. But I just want to clarify, the Prosecution has disclosed everything in our possession with regard to -- to the Milos reports. It doesn't matter whether they came from 1988 or 2001. I know that's an extended period, but we have disclosed everything that we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't -- it wasn't meant as a criticism of OTP. I was just explaining to the witness why am I show to go him the Milos report. And the Milos reports are only between 28th of July, 1991 and 1994, as -- as I understood the testimony of this witness. So it wasn't meant as a criticism.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let us go back to my question. This report that is in front of you, the one that you sent, do you doubt the veracity of facts listed there? Do you have any doubts concerning that? Was the information about that meeting held on the 10th of June, 1991, verified when the Council for National Security of the SDA was established?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely verified. This information was verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document be admitted into evidence, unless there's objections by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D278, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next document is 1D03-3437, tab 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, the CLSS has informed us that due to a large volume of documents, they are unable to translate this in time for today's session, but I assume that it will be translated by next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to object to these documents that are on the list of Defence that have not been translated. These documents versus been available to the Defence, I believe, for about a year now. They're not very long these Milos reports, as we've seen, and it is very difficult for me to follow along when I can only see a B/C/S version. Perhaps my learned friend could delay showing this witness this document until Monday if that -- maybe that perhaps is a solution, otherwise it is really difficult for myself and I assume the Trial Chamber as well to follow along. And I think that these reports were in their possession long enough that they could have this had them translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, what practical course would you suggest? Do you accept Mr. Olmsted's suggestion as being the way we should solve this problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I have to first comment on this. The Defence -- it is the truth that the Defence has in possession these documents for one year and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You notice I was trying to avoid asking you to respond to that, I don't want to get into who is responsible for what. I'm looking at a practical -- the -- the handicap, which Mr. Olmsted has identified, is perfectly understandable. As he said, the Trial Chamber is in the same position. So I'm trying to find a -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... well, Your Honours, I suggest the following course. I would ask the witness to confirm this document, the authenticity of this document. And I will only ask that it be admitted, as Mr. Olmsted did yesterday, on a list of documents once the -- the -- the translations are -- are -- are available.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I assume that that might create a problem for Mr. Olmsted for re-direct if we still don't have the -- the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So since it isn't it English, we would admit them on the list as you suggested but marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I -- it's up to Mr. Olmsted, if he has any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, how many documents are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe, Your Honours, we are missing translations of maybe seven or eight documents, not more than that. We received a number of maybe 25 in last two, three days, but these seven, eight are missing. They might be even available today, but I cannot guarantee because the CLSS complained that the deadlines were pretty short for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And you're satisfied that all seven of these are relevant, and you would wish to have all seven of them treated in the way that we've described.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's fine with the Prosecution so long as we have a chance to look at them and determine whether they're actually relevant to this case and make any objections before they're admitted. Otherwise we don't mind them being marked for identification at this stage at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Okay. So that is the course that we will proceed -- that we will -- that is the course that we would adopt. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I appreciate Your Honours' indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, this document is dated the 1st of March, 1992. This is a report by the Milos Group?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In this document, you give an overview of the situation.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a brief overview. A cross-section of the situation which, unfortunately, had terrible consequences in the village of Sijekovac near Bosanski Brod when a large number of Serbs were killed in a horrendous manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I think this was my original objection is that we don't want the Defence to lead evidence on a document we don't have translated and that they can mark it for identification for now but not lead evidence until we see the English translation. Without the English translation, there is no way we can determine whether he is accurately reflecting what's in the document, whether there's anything in there that is contrary to what is being asserted. It just makes it very impossible for us given the length of these document have been in their possession and their shortness, I think it's fair to the Prosecution that he certainly can mark them for identification now and come back to them on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I appreciate -- I appreciate what Mr. Olmsted said, except that I would assume that the Prosecution would be diligent enough to -- to translate all these documents because they had it in their possession for at least seven or eight years. But I will -- I will -- understanding the position of Mr. Olmsted, I will not ask the questions on -- on these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, please tell me, you were telling us about that tragic incident in the village of Sijekovac. It is a fact, isn't it, that in early 1992, the Republic of Croatia wanted to transfer the conflicts from its territory into the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina at any cost.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, with all due respect to you as a lawyer, you are now asking me to give my opinion. My opinion at this point in time is irrelevant. What is relevant is what I stated back in 1992, and that's precisely what I put back then, that there was a desire to transfer the problem from the territory of Croatia into the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask that this document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1D279, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 10185. Could this please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, before we comment on this document, let me ask you something. You are familiar with the genesis of the problem in Bosnia and Herzegovina, so I would rather not spend much time on it. Will you agree with me that in October 1991, a declaration was adopted at the Assembly, a declaration on independence and that it was done in a manner that represented a violation of the constitution?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then again in -- soon thereafter, Presidency and the government of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina asked the European Union to recognise the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Would you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You must know that, in late 1991, and in early 1992, European Union, wishing to resolve -- or, rather, to bring about a peaceful resolution of the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina established a commission and started negotiations, which were popularly known -- a commission and a plan, which were popularly known as the Cutileiro Plan, after the then minister of foreign affairs of Portugal who was in charge of those negotiations on behalf of the European Union?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm familiar with the plan and with the negotiations, and I remember well how it all ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The essence of the plan was that Bosnia and Herzegovina was to be split in three entities, with central organs of power which would remain in Sarajevo for all three entities, and then each entity individually, which were established on the basis of an ethnic principle, would have a large degree of autonomy, even when it comes to police affairs. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for reminding me, but I am quite familiar with that. And I also know who did not accept it. I'm just sparing you trouble if you wanted to clarify that. I don't want you to waste time on it, because I'm quite familiar with all of the events leading up to the breakout of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, isn't it, that representatives of all three national political parties accepted that agreement, then after some time had passed in late March, Mr. Izetbegovic withdrew his signature from that document. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, your report dated 6 March 1992 speaks of the fact that there is discontent among the employees of the public and state security, who were of Croat and Muslim background, due to their lack of agreement to work in a service that would have a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this report of yours speaks about the discontent among the employees of MUP, those who worked for public security and state security, and who were Croats and Muslims, because, according to your information, they did not want to work for a service which would have a larger degree of autonomy than the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 27, line 14, it shouldn't be "than" it should be "from;" that they would have a larger degree of autonomy from MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, it is a fact that back on the 6th of March, 1992, there was some discussion about how the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina would split into three MUPs for each -- for each entity in accordance with this EU plan?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And you have to understand that the employees of the National Security Service were informed about this much better on average than your regular citizen or your regular employee of the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, could this be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D280, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, it is a fact, isn't it, that, at that time, the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina didn't function in a regular way -- or, rather, there were some divisions along ethnic lines, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I was there. I walked the ground. I was out on the field. And the situation was that of great confusion. So, in March and in April, already an employee of the public security could not freely move in the territory of Gracanica, let alone Maglaj, Tesanj. There were always barricades erected there already. Everything was coloured there along ethnic lines and affiliations. In the statement and in my evidence yesterday, I stated quite clearly, and can I repeat it now, that I gave only one, 67 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, the interpreter needs -- Mr. Radulovic, the interpreter requires you to repeat a portion of your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may be of assistance, because I understood, maybe I could lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, would you please correct me: You're trying to say that back while giving evidence over the last few day, you said that only one-third of your report, of your documents and information is here in this case, was presented in this case which is 33 per cent; whereas, 67 per cent of your work product is not represented in the documents here, and that pertains to what members of other ethnic groups did in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina in late 1991 and early 1992. It also pertains to how they were organised and armed.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. You just said late 1991 and early 1992, but my data goes back to 1987, and we should not overlook these three years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't want to underestimate it, but I explained to you, that, unfortunately, we don't have these documents. Tell me, sir, the State Security Service at the time, and I'm referring to late 1991 and early 1992, was headed by Mr. Branko Kvesic; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at the level of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, yes. As far as I remember, yes, he did. He was relatively briefly in that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You as a long-standing member of state security certainly will know that the SDB, figuratively speaking, was -- had as many holes as a sieve, and confidential information would be given to the media, ethnic parties, individuals and without authorisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct. And if I may add, the SDB was divided along ethnic lines. The SDB members who were Bosniaks worked in the interest of the SDA; Croats, in the interest of the HDZ; and some of the Serbs worked for the SDS. But there were still shows who believed in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and didn't signed with any of -- didn't side with any of these counts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, isn't it, that at the headquarters of the SDB in Sarajevo, in administration 01, to which you belonged, that there were only Muslims there as staff, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This transformation was observed in 1990, and there was no one Serb left in the intelligence administration, which was a clear indication of something. And whoever knew the intelligence culture could draw his conclusions that something was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There's still some time, so tell me about this document that we see here. On the 7th of March, you speak about the MUP leadership decided to have 100 employees retired, mostly Serbs, and hire 250 Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that document on my screen. But I remember the contents. You have reminded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I asked for document 1D03-3349 to be displayed. The document is dated 7 March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which tab was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Perhaps we should pick this up after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, a couple of things. First, I would like to express my apology to the interpreters, that's one thing, and I promise that I will make sure that I control myself and control the witness as much as I can. That's one thing. The second thing, we have received some translations in the course of -- of the trial and it's been uploaded at the moment. However, I talked to my friend, Mr. Olmsted, from the -- from the Office of the Prosecutor, and we -- we basically agreed that Mr. Olmsted would not have a problem if I offer some of the documents exactly the same -- the same way as -- as he did yesterday, on assumption that all these documents are Milos reports and that I don't need to -- to authenticate them with the witness. I think it would shorten the time considerably of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Olmsted can verify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That's fine with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic, before Mr. Zecevic continues, I would just wish to remind you that your evidence has -- your testimony has to be interpreted, so if you could remember to slow down in your answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honours. I will try.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We took the break when we were dealing with this document, 1D03-3349. My question to you was about the contents of this document, and I read it to you. Could you confirm to us the facts mentioned here so we may continue?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the Milos Group. The contents were implemented partly later. The motivation is also mentioned here. And -- well, that would be it in a nutshell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D281, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could we please see 1D03-3353. Is this a Milos document?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In accordance with what has been agreed between the OTP and the Defence, I would like to have this document marked for identification until we receive a translation. This is tab 8. The document is 1D03-3353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D282, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you, you lived in Banja Luka, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the SDA and the HDZ in the Banja Luka territory wanted that new municipalities be established in that territory?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I wrote about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Among others, there were the municipalities of Stari Grad and some others, or -- including parts of Banja Luka, where the majority of the population was Muslim or Croatian, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Among others, Ivanjska, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vrbanja, Ivanjska, Stari Grad, almost all neighbourhoods where Bosniaks and Croats were the majority. And where it was possible to establish new municipalities, there was such demands, such interests, and attempts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 1D03-3363, tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this report dated 25 March 1992? This is also about a Milos Group report. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this report?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Here, you mention information about the intentions of the paramilitary units of the Croatian Defence Council to attack some of the municipalities of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 25th or 26th of March, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I must tell you, unfortunately, this report, as many others, was disregarded to a great extent. On the 25th, the 26th, and the 27th, HOS units attacked Sijekovac and massacred the people there, which means that our report preceded the events, which shows that we did good operative work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You're saying that your report dated 25 March -- or, rather, that what was mentioned in your report dated 25 March came true two days later?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D283, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, that the chief of the SDB of the CSB of Banja Luka, Mr. Kesic, round about February or March 1992 went to an attend a meeting in Sarajevo at Bruno Kvesic's office, the then subsecretary for the State Security Service, and, on that occasion, brought back a Golf vehicle for the SDB of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. But I think his first name was not Bruno, it was Branko. I don't remember that detail. But I know that at that time, the first half, that is, Mr. Kvesic went to meetings -- to attend meetings in Sarajevo. I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Mr. Kesic, your chief of SDB in Banja Luka, complained to you that in Brane Kvesic's office, that is the office of the subsecretary of the SDB in Sarajevo, he saw a Croatian flag, or the rather, the flag of the HDZ rather than the flag of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember such stories which I heard from Mr. Kesic. He was on good terms with us, and I remember not only these details but also other details which he found extremely surprising. And he said that the situation in the SDB was total chaos. That is more or less what I remember from those conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 34, line 19, the name should be Kesic, rather than Kvesic. That's the gentleman from Banja Luka who went to attend meetings at Kvesic's office in Sarajevo. The surnames are very similar so that's probably why.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember another detail concerning this meeting that Kesic attended in Sarajevo and which he may have related to you; namely, that on that occasion, Brano Kvesic said to him that the SDB of BiH is falling apart and that he would go to Mostar to work for the MUP of Herceg-Bosna, and he said to Kesic, You go back to Banja Luka and take this Golf. Do you remember the detail?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember all of it except for the Golf. I could have continued to say the same thing that you said. I remember him saying that Branko Kvesic was very open with regard to the security situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and, actually, this frankness of his was surprising.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, your chief of the SDB in Banja Luka, related that to you in early 1992, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you about a document, sir, which was shown to you two days ago, I believe. It's document P1366. It's another report of the Milos Group. You commented on it with my learned friend from the Prosecution. I have some additional questions. It refers to the documentation on the war organisation of the Banja Luka CSB. You remember discussing this document?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, Mr. Radulovic, isn't it, that these defence plans of the MUP and its organisational units, that is, SJBs, and CSBs, that these plans were made in accordance with the Law on All People's Defence and social self-protection. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the said law, you will agree with me, each of the institutions of the former Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia was duty-bound to adopt or prepare a so-called defence plan for situations of wartime or immediate threat of war. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These facts are well known.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When I speak of all institution, I refer also to schools, universities, hospitals, companies. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only will I agree with you, these are facts, well-known facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I think it was the day before yesterday, but I'm not sure, you discussed with my friend from the Prosecution events of the 3rd of April, 1992, when members of the SOS group blockaded the city of Banja Luka. Do you remember this discussion?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I remember the discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, it is a fact that on that day, the 3rd of April, 1992, the VRS, the Army of the Republika Srpska, did not exist, that at the time that the federal army, JNA, was still present in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that events that triggered this blockade of Banja Luka was a statement made by the minister of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Jerko Doko. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the statement made by Jerko Doko, but I do remember that it was something related to preparing resistance for the events that was supposed to come. Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you elaborate a bit. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, institutions and organs in the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina failed. It was a state of chaos. Without such a state, there wouldn't have been paramilitary and other formations, and if I may add, the crucial part in the chaos was played by the members of the JNA who were, so to speak, nowhere between heaven and earth. They were in the territory but they were not under the authority of the executive organs of the relevant republics. They didn't know how to handle the situation. Had they known, Yugoslavia wouldn't have fallen apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to try and remind you, Mr. Jerko Doko, who was at the time minister of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 2nd of April, stated for the TV and other media that all conscripts and reserve troops who should take part in the units of JNA and who are citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and if they are involved in the fighting in the Republic of Croatia, are actually conducting a private war and that they will be asked to show whether they are responsible for that. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember when this was broadcast, but I do remember reactions to these statements of his, namely, parents, especially mothers of mobilised soldiers or soldiers who were, at the time, in the JNA and were members of either Croat or Bosniak people organised rallies in front of basic offices of Secretariats of National Defence in municipalities, asking for their children to be withdrawn, to be demobilized. There were even some situations that were dangerous. There was -- there were involvement of some active soldiers there to try and prevent that because mothers tried to use force and enter the archives of the secretariat and burn all the documents related to mobilisation. I remember that the regional centres and some military commands took out the documentation. It was taken out by the relevant authorities to prevent them from being destroyed. I know a lot about these events, so I'm elaborating. I hope that everyone in the courtroom knows about the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The crux of my question had to do with the following: Do you remember that this statement by Jerko Doko was one of the reasons which SOS gave as their explanation for the blockade of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you asked me about my opinion. If you're asking me to give you my opinion, I can tell you that in the context of all the other events, this also had a part. Now whether it had a -- the most important part or the secondary level importance, well, I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that in the course of your conversation with the Prosecution you were told that there is an linkage between the events in Sarajevo, namely, setting up of barricades in Sarajevo on the 1st of March, 1991, and -- correction, 1992, and blockade of Banja Luka on the 30th of June -- on 3rd of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that all your questions I read as something that is part of your interest, but you cannot put to me anything that I would not agree with and then that I agree with that. That would be silly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact that the two events were caused by completely different sets of events?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, since you were a member of the service and since you -- your field of expertise was intelligence, you were shown at the very beginning of our today's session a video recording of the parade that took place on the 13th of May. It is a -- it is true, isn't it, that the day of security services, 13th of May, was something that was celebrated for years before 1992 and that the celebrations were similar. There was a programme, a parade, people would gather. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's the day when these services were formed in 1994 [as interpreted], when OSNA was formed, and since 1944, celebrations were held until 1992. It was a holiday. People would gather together, enjoy themselves.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction to the transcript, it wasn't in 1994, it was in 1944.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact that, on that day, the 13th of May, the Assembly of the Serbian people was also -- its session was held in Banja Luka -- or, rather, of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, on that very day?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, I'm sorry. I'm not trying to evade answering your question, but there were so many events taking place, I can't remember whether it was held on the same day or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: OTP said that you had an opportunity to review the footage, and part of the broadcast included mention of the Assembly session being held in Banja Luka. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But when you ask me about whether I remember that, I don't remember it. I do remember having seen it on the video, but I cannot confirm that I remember the events from 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were shown one part of the introductory speech made by the minister at the time, Mico Stanisic, which included a report on the security situation in the territory of the republic -- Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since the video material included only one segment of this address of his, let me ask you whether you remember that at the time or immediately prior to that the incident did take place on the St. George's Day in Srebrenica when the Muslim armed forces attacked and killed some of the Serbian inhabitants there. Do you know that on the basis of your operative information?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I knew much more about that at the time than the minister, Mico Stanisic, told the address -- told the people gathered there, and it is what -- what he said was absolutely true. In this shortened version of his address were correct, but the events in the area of Srebrenica were much more tragic than what Mr. Stanisic said about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can confirm, then, the part of his statement where he had said that service has information according to which members of Serbian people are used as human shields around certain facilities?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I can even tell you in which areas and to what degree -- or, rather, how many of people were used as human shields. But, of course, Mico Stanisic - and I hope he won't take it against me if I say this - didn't know about all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember a part of his address -- I'm saying this because the sound of the video-clip was not very good. But do you remember the part of his address where Mr. Mico Stanisic criticises or points out that there is trend of establishing so-called private armies, threatening not only the Serbian people but members of all ethnicities living in the area of Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. But I'm afraid that this sentence that was uttered by Mr. Mico Stanisic is something that could be found in one of our reports, one of the Milos Group reports. And that's a reason why I would want to say that we, intelligence group Milos, contributed to informing Mr. Mico Stanisic in a proper way. It is impossible that it was just a coincidence that the same sentence was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when we discussed your reports, you told us that the Milos Group reports were submitted in two different forms.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, to two addresses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When I said "in two different forms," I referred to a shorter dispatch form and a longer detailed form, which was a report.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. I apologise. I started answering before having heard you completely. Yes, there were two forms, which deferred by the extent of the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D03-3391 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is your report dated the 23rd of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this would be the dispatch form, a shorter report.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Earlier on, you said that it was sent to two recipients. The first recipient was the SDB of Serbia; and the second one was your immediate superior, Vojin Bera, the chief of department number 01 within the Banja Luka CSB.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, earlier on you told us that you recognised the typewriter, because of its special features, the typewriter used to type these reports.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this is precisely how your report, the one submitted to Vojin Bera, looked like?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this pertains to all of the reports you -- that were put to you here?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These reports were typed up on a sheet of paper, and then, in that form, they were submitted to your immediate superior, Mr. Bera?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zecevic, please don't say sheet of paper, because I don't know how else one can type up a report. There's no other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you submitted your reports on a daily basis, and sometimes several times a day.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic. Sometimes there were a dozen of such reports or pieces of information provided in one shape or another, be it as a dispatch or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "in one shape or another," either as a dispatch or as a report, you are still referring to a typed-up document?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I remember well the conversation that you and I had, you said that you kept your records of the Milos reports - and we can see that each of them is numbered, at least far as I could see - and that you kept this record in a special log that was in your safe box?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. We had an internal log-book. How else would these reports emerge had they not been left and kept in the safe deposit box? We always submitted one copy and then kept one copy for us, because our numbers, our registration numbers, did not correspond with the registration numbers in the main log-book which was kept within the head office of the department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So your internal records, your internal log-book that was kept in your safe deposit box was not shown to you. You don't even know whether it exists?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened with that log-book. But what nobody has managed to find was the dossiers of our collaborators and friendly contacts because I put it in a safe place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, isn't it, that Mr. Bera did not keep a separate log-book for the reports he received from you.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for a fact that he did not have a separate log-book, separate records for that. Rather, he registered our information on the time of their arrival. And then prior to that number, there would be number 10 or 20, depending on how many reports were sent on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see that general log-book, as you call it, after leaving the Banja Luka State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see that log-book after I left, and I also never saw it even while I worked for the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you well, your claim that it was registered in the log-book is your assumption. You said this, assuming that this is how all reports were registered, but you don't know that for a fact, but you did not see that general log-book either while you still worked there, or afterwards.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, since the reports of the Milos Group, which had been established in July of 1991, were sent, do you know whether the chief of your administration, and also the chief of State Security Service, Mr. Kesic, ever sent your reports to the seat of the State Security Service in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know whether they sent all reports and to what extent or whether they made a selection. I have no idea how my superiors treated my reports, whether they forwarded them or not, and how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know whether they re-worked your reports and included them in some other reports. You have no idea what they did with your reports.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In your evidence here, you said several times -- I apologise. I will get back to that later. In the meantime, we still have the document on our screens. You saw this document and you confirmed it was yours?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I notice something that was quite interesting to me. In the third sentence of the document, you say: "Based on our previous experience and according to what we know, these departures were observed as a rule, immediately prior to armed operations by Ustasha units and Green Berets." In the previous text you say that a large number of citizens was moving out of the Teslic municipality and then you go on to say that this type of departures en masse were typical on the eve of armed attacks of the enemy?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please clarify this.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
